ai.definition: Consciousness Simulation refers to a theoretical and experimental approach aimed at simulating human consciousness using advanced computational methods. This technology seeks to understand the nature of consciousness by creating models that can replicate its key aspects, with potential applications in developing AI systems that exhibit similar qualities.
ai.howItWorks: The process involves modeling neural networks and other brain structures using quantum computing techniques, which are believed to offer greater computational power for complex simulations. These simulations aim to capture the emergent properties of consciousness, such as awareness and subjective experience.
ai.problemSolved: Current AI lacks true understanding or subjective experiences, limiting its capabilities in tasks requiring human-like judgment or creativity.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing quantum computing hardware capable of handling complex neural simulations. This includes the design and fabrication of qubits and quantum circuits, as well as software development for simulation algorithms.
ai.buildProcess: Building a consciousness simulation system requires integrating advanced computational techniques with neuroscientific data to create accurate models. The process is highly experimental and relies on interdisciplinary collaboration between computer scientists, physicists, and neuroscientists.
ai.costDrivers: High costs are driven by the need for cutting-edge quantum computing infrastructure, specialized software development, and extensive data collection from brain studies.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is in its early stages of development and faces significant challenges before it can be practically implemented.
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations governing consciousness simulation. However, as the technology advances, ethical considerations related to AI and brain modeling will likely lead to new regulatory frameworks.
ai.risks: Technical risks include the difficulty in accurately modeling complex neural processes and ensuring that simulations do not inadvertently create sentient entities. Ethical concerns revolve around the potential misuse of such technology or the unintended consequences of creating artificial consciousness.
ai.profitability: Given its current stage, there is no clear path to profitability. Potential future applications could drive value but are speculative at this point.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving quantum computing capabilities and refining simulation techniques to better capture the nuances of human consciousness.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units would draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and cryogenic cooling. Quantum computers require significant amounts of power for operation and maintenance.

A class of machine learning algorithms inspired by the structure and function of biological neural networks, used for tasks like pattern recognition and decision making.

subsystems.name: Brain mapping
subsystems.role: recovering the wiring diagram — which neuron connects to which, and how strongly.

subsystems.name: Activity recording
subsystems.role: measuring what real neurons actually do while an animal behaves.

subsystems.name: Neuron models
subsystems.role: mathematical descriptions of how a single cell integrates inputs and fires.

subsystems.name: Simulation engine
subsystems.role: runs billions of model neurons in step with each other.

subsystems.name: Validation and comparison
subsystems.role: checks simulated activity against the biological original.

subsystems.name: Consciousness assay
subsystems.role: attempts to decide whether the simulation is merely behaving intelligently or is actually experiencing something.

buildSteps.title: Fix and slice tissue
buildSteps.detail: Brain tissue is preserved, stained and cut into nanometre-thin sections, then imaged slice by slice at electron-microscope resolution.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the wiring
buildSteps.detail: Machine-learning segmentation traces each neuron's branches through the image stack and marks every synapse, producing a graph of the network.

buildSteps.title: Record living activity
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes or calcium indicators are used in the living animal to log firing patterns during defined tasks, giving a reference for what the network does.

buildSteps.title: Fit cell models
buildSteps.detail: Each class of neuron is given equations matching its measured electrical behaviour, including how connections strengthen or weaken with use.

buildSteps.title: Instantiate the network
buildSteps.detail: The connectome graph and cell models are loaded into a simulator, and the model is stepped forward in time on a supercomputer or neuromorphic hardware.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop on the body
buildSteps.detail: The simulated brain is wired to a simulated or robotic body with sensors and muscles, so it can act and receive consequences of its actions.

buildSteps.title: Validate against biology
buildSteps.detail: Simulated firing is compared with the recorded original under the same stimuli; mismatches drive model revision.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Once a small network matches, the same pipeline is repeated for larger brains — the cost grows roughly with the number of neurons and synapses, so each step is a large jump in compute.

buildSteps.title: Probe for experience
buildSteps.detail: The system is perturbed and its responses compared with predictions from competing theories of consciousness; no method yet gives a definitive answer.

pathway.milestone: complete maps and simulations of very small nervous systems, plus large models of cortical circuits
pathway.unlocks: methods for tracing, modelling and validating networks.

pathway.milestone: behaviourally faithful simulation of a small mammal's brain regions
pathway.unlocks: a testbed for comparing theories of consciousness against real data.

pathway.milestone: primate-scale partial emulation with perturbation-based assays
pathway.unlocks: empirical evidence about which brain structures are needed for subjective experience — if any assay can be trusted.
